picked.t: Sun Group, Visa partner to develop digital tourism services in Vietnam
picked.body: The agreement was signed during the official visit to the U.S. by General Secretary and State President To Lam and a high-level Vietnamese delegation. The partnership combines Sun Group's tourism and hospitality businesses with Visa's payment network and technology, covering destination promotion, customer experience, loyalty programs, technology and data, payments, and international marketing. Phu Quoc, which is set to host the APEC 2027 Economic Leaders' Meeting, is a key focus. Under the agreement, Sun Group will explore participation in Visa Destinations, which could promote its accommodation, dining, entertainment and other tourism services to Visa cardholders worldwide before they travel to Vietnam. The companies will use Visa's global platforms, media channels and international content creator network to promote Vietnamese destinations, focusing on eight priority markets: South Korea, Japan, mainland China, Taiwan (China), India, Australia, Singapore and Malaysia. The partnership builds on their existing collaboration on Visit Vietnam, part of the national digital tourism ecosystem developed and operated by Sun Group, with government support and in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the National Data Association (NDA). The two businesses plan to develop Visit Vietnam through new payment services, joint marketing, data collaboration and initiatives supporting the tourism sector's digital transformation. They will also explore integrating Visa Destinations into the platform. The partnership aligns with Resolution No. 26-NQ/TW of the Politburo, which calls for smart tourism services, national tourism databases and digital platforms, as well as wider adoption of e-commerce, cashless payments and cross-border payment services. This partnership is taking shape at a time when digital transformation has become a major national priority for Vietnam. On same day in New York, General Secretary and President To Lam met with Robert (Bobby) Thomson, Senior Vice President, Global Head of Government Affairs, Visa, to discuss expanding cooperation in digital transformation and digital payments. General Secretary and President To Lam called on Visa to work with Vietnamese partners to build a digital tourism ecosystem, enhance the visitor experience, and create a seamless digital journey for travelers. According to Sun Group, this is also the direction of the company and Visa pursuing through Visit Vietnam, connecting key touchpoints across the digital travel journey, from destination discovery and service experiences to payments. Building on their existing partnership, both parties are well positioned to translate this vision into scalable initiatives that deliver tangible value for travelers and contribute to the digital transformation of Vietnam's tourism industry. Dung Dang, Visa Country Manager for Vietnam and Laos, said technology, data and secure payments are playing an increasingly important role in how travelers discover and experience destinations. "Our partnership with Sun Group brings together complementary strengths—from destination development and hospitality to global payments technology and insights—to create new ways for travelers to experience Vietnam," she said. "By combining our capabilities, we aim to support Vietnam's ambition to become a more digitally enabled, globally connected, and high-value tourism destination, while creating greater opportunities for businesses and travelers alike." Focus on Phu Quoc The two partners will explore payment solutions for delegates and visitors to APEC 2027, integrate destination services and promote Phu Quoc across APEC economies. They also plan to develop a digital payments roadmap for infrastructure supporting the event, including potential contactless payment services on the island's light rail transit (LRT) system. Beyond destination promotion and payments, the companies plan to expand customer benefits, particularly for premium cardholders and international travelers. They will launch the Sun Signature Visa Infinite Private card, combining payment services with travel and lifestyle benefits for high-net-worth customers. Sun Group's premium travel, hospitality and lifestyle offerings will also be integrated into Visa's global benefits network, giving eligible Visa cardholders access to selected experiences and destinations in Vietnam. Through the Visa Rewards Platform, they will also examine opportunities for Sun Signature members to transfer or exchange points with participating loyalty programs and partners. Visa cardholders and eligible loyalty-program members may in turn be able to redeem points for Sun Group's travel, hospitality and entertainment services. Dang Minh Truong, Chairman of Sun Group, said the partnership comes as Vietnam places greater emphasis on tourism development and digital platforms. picked.t: From desks to dusting: Office workers take on cleaning side jobs
picked.body: The 24-year-old works in corporate marketing but takes house-cleaning shifts through an online platform to help pay for foreign language courses and professional training. She attends classes twice a week and cleans homes three evenings a week. Each three-hour cleaning shift pays more than VND200,000 (US$8). She picks up extra shifts on weekends when she has no plans with friends. Cleaning brings in about VND4 million a month, which, combined with her office salary, covers rent and utilities and helps her make ends meet in Ho Chi Minh City, where the cost of living is the fourth-highest in the country. "Should I go in or turn back?" Tram wondered six months ago, standing outside a customer’s home before her first shift. After hesitating for more than five minutes, she picked up her bag of cleaning supplies and rang the doorbell of the two-story house. The homeowner was used to middle-aged women doing the cleaning and was surprised to see a Gen Z woman at the door. The work has become easier as Tram has grown used to wearing rubber gloves and learned which cleaning products to use on floors and which are only for glass. What she values most is that the job is "mentally undemanding." Once the house is clean, she can leave and get paid immediately. She could also supplement her income with marketing work, but that would probably keep her at her computer until late at night. "Eight hours at the office handling tasks, emails, messages and conversations with clients is more than enough," she said. Tram’s choice of manual work after office hours is not unusual, as more workers seek second jobs to supplement their incomes. Applicants for hourly cleaning shifts are getting younger, with many under 45, said a woman who works in partnership development at JupViec, an app for booking hourly cleaning services. Many work in offices, teach, sell real estate or run small businesses. Others are students. They typically take three to five shifts a week, choosing evenings or days off. Each shift lasts two to three hours and involves housecleaning, with no cooking required. The schedule allows them to earn extra money around work or school while leaving time to see friends and care for their families and children. People with regular jobs are drawn to the extra income and the chance to try flexible work without a long-term commitment, said Lai Thi Duy Hong, a team leader overseeing more than 100 people registered for hourly housekeeping work. Some workers ages 35 to 40 are also financing their "backup plan." They are preparing for a career change once they are past the age recruiters tend to favor and find it harder to stay with a company over the long term. How long they continue cleaning depends on why they started. Some stay for three to six months, while many keep doing it for two or three years. "Most have to get past their pride and their reservations about doing manual work alongside their regular jobs before they can settle in," Hong said. "This is a service business, and customer ratings are how their performance is measured." "Hourly cleaning is much like the housework we do every day. Instead of spending all our time on unpaid chores, it makes more sense to find a way to earn money from them," said Khanh Huyen, a corporate accountant. The 38-year-old was not under much financial pressure when she began cleaning homes nearly four months ago. She was going through a stressful period and wanted to keep herself physically busy so she would not have to think so much. After more than a decade in an office, Huyen had grown tired of sitting at a computer working with numbers and documents. She chose manual work because she considered cleaning a hobby. Her first few shifts felt like a race against the clock: she had just two hours to clean every room, including the bathrooms. At home, she could let a few spots slide. On the job, she had to be meticulous to avoid poor customer ratings. After several shifts, Huyen settled into the routine. She now earns an extra VND3 million ($115) to VND5 million a month by working four or five shifts a week. Each pays VND170,000 to VND250,000, depending on the workload. "The side job eases a lot of my stress, and sometimes meeting homeowners who treat me well makes me happy," she said. The work has also given Huyen a new perspective on this part of the service industry and taught her things beyond accounting. Manual work has taught Tram more than she expected, too. Regular conversations with homeowners have made her less hesitant to talk to strangers. Sometimes, cleaning becomes enjoyable as she chats with a homeowner while helping prepare ingredients for a meal. Working on deep cleans with older female colleagues has taught her to distinguish between cleaning chemicals and use them without damaging household items. She has also gained more experience handling household chores. Tram sees cleaning as a temporary way to supplement her income and remains determined to focus on her main job.

picked.t: HCMC set to begin construction of 3 new metro lines for $9.6B
picked.body: The Thu Dau Mot - Tao Dan, Tan Son Nhat - Phu Huu and Binh Duong New City - Suoi Tien metro lines, are expected to break ground in the fourth quarter of this year. The Ho Chi Minh City Urban Railway Management Board, which oversees all metro projects in the city, announced on Sept. 21 that it is working with consultants to complete feasibility studies and procedures for the three lines before submitting them to the authorities for approval. All are expected to be funded by the government. If completed by 2030 as planned, they will help the city's urban rail network to around 255 km by the end of the decade. The Thu Dau Mot - Tao Dan metro line will be the longest and have the highest price tag at more than 33 km and an estimated cost of VND113 trillion. It will start near Hung Vuong Street in Binh Duong Ward and run along Pham Ngoc Thach Street, Binh Duong Boulevard, National Highway 13, and Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street before entering central HCMC. It will have 24 stations, including 13 underground, and a depot in Hiep Binh Phuoc. The final station at Tao Dan Park will be an interchange in the city center with the Ben Thanh - Tham Luong metro line, or line No. 2, which is now under construction. The second line is the first phase of Metro Line No. 6, from Tan Son Nhat to Phu Huu, which will span around 23 km and have a cost of VND86 trillion. The line is expected to have 17 stations, including 13 underground and four elevated stations, with a depot in Binh Trieu. The line will pass through Tan Son Nhat airport with two underground stations before heading toward the city's eastern area. Once completed, it will connect Tan Son Nhat with the metro network and the Thu Thiem - Long Thanh railway, forming a mass-transit corridor between the two airports. The remaining line will connect Binh Duong New City with Suoi Tien, stretching nearly 31 km with a cost of around VND55 trillion. It will start near the A1 Roundabout in Binh Duong Ward and run through Phu Loi, Thuan Giao, An Phu, Tan Dong Hiep, Di An and Dong Hoa. The first phase is expected to have 17 stations. In the Dong Hoa - Tan Van area, the line will connect with the existing metro network and railway lines toward Dong Nai and Long Thanh Airport. HCMC currently operates nearly 20 km of the Ben Thanh - Suoi Tien metro line. The city aims to expand its urban railway network to around 255 km by 2030. Since the beginning of the year, the city has started construction or held groundbreaking ceremonies for three projects: Ben Thanh - Tham Luong, Ben Thanh - Thu Thiem and Ben Thanh - Can Gio. In addition to the three other state-funded lines being prepared for investment, the city is also accelerating work on the Thu Thiem - Long Thanh railway and Metro Line No. 2's Tham Luong - An Ha - Northwest Urban Area section.

picked.t: Miss World Vanessa Ponce explores Hanoi by motorbike, tries street food
picked.body: The Miss World event began in early September, and the beauty chose to explore Hanoi during her free time, documenting her experiences with local food and everyday life in a series of vlogs that have drawn attention from fans. The Mexican said she had wanted to visit Vietnam for years but only now got the opportunity. Her interest grew after watching programs by the late American chef and documentary filmmaker Anthony Bourdain, whose advice to "be a traveler, not a tourist" resonated with her. Vietnam was among the countries Bourdain spoke fondly of. Ponce de León tried Vietnamese coffee and iced tea at street-side stalls in the Old Quarter. She described Vietnamese coffee as strong and said iced tea appeared to be an integral part of daily life. She joked that the best seats in Hanoi are often made of plastic and sit just 15 centimeters above the ground. In another vlog, León documents a day exploring the Old Quarter, visiting an art exhibition, trying grilled pork with rice vermicelli bun cha, banh mi , and steamed rice rolls banh cuon , and traveling by motorbike taxi. "Recording from Vietnam: the people, bun cha , Vietnamese fashion, getting swept up in beautiful things and, inevitably, a motorbike ride. Just another ordinary day in Hanoi," she writes in the caption. After exploring the capital, she traveled to Sa Pa, dressed casually, posing for photos with locals, and trying traditional clothing worn by ethnic people in the northern highlands. In 2018, León, who stands 1.74 meters tall, became the first Mexican to win the Miss World title. She was the winner of the 2014 "Mexico's Next Top Model". She works as a model, presenter, and speaker and has been involved in social and community projects supporting indigenous children, migrants, and people with disabilities.

picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City rules out gasoline vehicle ban, bets on free buses and EV incentives instead
picked.body: At the meeting in Quang's National Assembly constituency, voter Phan Thi Ngoc Huong said congestion was spreading from the city's gateways and arterial roads into many other areas. She also urged the city to carefully assess the shift from gasoline to electric vehicles, saying it would directly affect people's lives, especially workers and low-income earners. "We will not ban people from using gasoline vehicles," Quang said in response. The city will instead study economic and financial policies to encourage the switch, possibly with different rules for different areas. Smart cameras could identify vehicles so electric vehicle users receive incentives and priority while gasoline vehicles face separate policies, he said. The cost of the transition could be shared among the state, residents and businesses, allowing the switch to happen gradually rather than all at once. Quang cited China, where some areas give electric vehicles priority so they travel faster. People there can park gasoline vehicles outside restricted zones and continue their journeys on electric ones. Quang said congestion is harder to solve in HCMC than elsewhere because of its large population. Working hours and daily routines are concentrated, sending vehicles onto the roads at the same time in the morning and afternoon. No single measure can fix it, he added, calling for a mix of public transport, regulation of private vehicles, technology and a change in traffic culture. "The first solution is public transport in place of private vehicles," he said, noting that the city had set aside more than VND2 trillion (US$77 million) to make bus rides free for a year. The fare waiver took effect on July 1 on 134 intra-city routes and is currently set to run through Dec. 31, at an estimated cost of VND630 billion ($24 million). The routes carried more than 26.8 million passengers from July 1 to Sept. 22, up 48% year-on-year, according to the city's Public Transport Management Center. The city will deploy larger buses at peak hours and smaller ones when demand is low, using technology to match capacity to demand. Buses will also be reorganized to feed passengers to the expanding metro network, while bus stops and passenger facilities are upgraded. Drivers who squeeze into any gap on the road regardless of the rules disrupt traffic flow and make jams worse, Quang said. "Traffic congestion is one of the four tasks the Party General Secretary assigned to HCMC at the city Party Congress," he said. The city aims for public transport to meet 15-20% of travel demand by 2030. HCMC is also studying restrictions on private vehicles by area and time slot. A draft plan by the city's Department of Construction proposes piloting a low-emission zone from July 2027 in the central core and Thu Thiem, then expanding it to Ring Road 2 from early 2029. Private motorbikes would need to be electric or green-powered to enter the zone by 2035.

picked.t: 221 passengers evacuate Air Seoul flight to Vietnam after fire breaks out in bag, power bank suspected
picked.body: Smoke began rising from a bag a passenger had stowed under a seat on flight RS511 at around 9 p.m. local time and soon turned into a fire, according to Air Seoul. The bag held a power bank kept in a pouch, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. Crew members put out the flames using bottled water and other means before firefighters arrived to check on passengers, The Chosun Ilbo reported. Some passengers complained of breathing discomfort, but none needed hospital treatment and no injuries were reported. The aircraft had 228 people on board, including seven crew members. Many of the passengers were families heading to the central Vietnamese city for Chuseok, South Korea's autumn harvest holiday. Air Seoul had everyone leave the plane and brought in another aircraft so the original could undergo safety checks. The replacement flight took off about two hours and 50 minutes late with 219 passengers, after two chose not to travel. Air Seoul and fire authorities are still working to determine the cause. The passenger had taken measures to prevent the battery from short-circuiting, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. Some passengers have suggested the fire started while the power bank was being used to charge an e-cigarette. Air Seoul said it presumes the power bank caught fire but is "still verifying the facts, including whether it was in use," The Chosun Ilbo reported. Since April 20, South Korea has limited air passengers to two power banks each and banned using or recharging them on board, under rules it drafted and the International Civil Aviation Organization adopted as a global standard. Passengers must keep the batteries with them, sealed in a bag or insulated, and not in overhead bins, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. The rules followed a January 2025 fire that destroyed an Air Busan jet at Gimhae International Airport in Busan after a power bank stored in an overhead bin ignited.

picked.t: Students dread losing edge after slog as Vietnam mulls over scrapping IELTS bonus points for university entry
picked.body: Hong Minh, a 12th-grader in Ho Chi Minh City, was shocked that the 6.5 IELTS score she earned following two years of preparation might no longer give her an edge while applying for university admission. She began preparing for IELTS while still in 10th grade to improve her chances of admission to the political science or international relations majors at the University of Social Sciences and Humanities, Vietnam National University. During its most recent admissions, the university did not convert IELTS scores into English subject scores but only awarded three bonus points out of 100 to applicants with an IELTS score of 5.5 or higher. The 100 comprised academic performance, which includes high school graduation exam scores, academic transcripts, and competency assessment results, in addition to bonus and priority points. "Since I don't qualify for any priority points, I chose the IELTS certificate to compete," Minh said. Now, the education ministry is proposing that, from 2027, only regional and beneficiary-group priority points will remain and not bonus points for achievements or certificates . Bonus points for certificates such as IELTS are currently capped at 1.5 out of 30 as a general rule, but each university, such as HCMC University of Social Sciences and Humanities, sets its own rules, as long as it stays under the cap. "The certificate I worked so hard to obtain could become useless for admission," Minh said. High-school students now take a uniform national graduation exams comprising math, literature, and two electives. Universities use a combined score of three subjects, depending on the major applied by students, for admissions. Each university has its own admission standards and has, for years, been allowed to award additional points to applicants for academic awards, language certificates such as IELTS or SAT, and extracurricular achievements. Under the ministry's proposal, students will only receive priority points based on their residential area or eligibility under preferential policies for disadvantaged students, children of martyrs and veterans, and ethnic minorities. Those residing in remote localities will receive 0.25-0.75 points added to their scores. Nguyen Hoang, a 12th grader in Hanoi, began preparing for IELTS a year ago. While he has not decided which major or university to apply to, he said he had found from looking at admission policies over the past two years that IELTS could boost his admission score, particularly as the high school graduation exam is now designed to distinguish more clearly between students at different ability levels, making perfect scores more and more difficult to achieve. He said scoring a 9 in the English exam would be "very difficult," while getting an 8 and adding another 1-1.5 points with an IELTS 6.5 certificate is within his reach. "That's why I invested in IELTS. Now that the bonus points could be scrapped, I don't know what to do." The ministry says awarding bonus points for international certificates "could create inequality" because access to such certificates depends on economic conditions, place of residence--with students living in urban areas getting access IELTS centers more easily, and families' financial abilities. The change would have a strong impact on 11th and 12th graders who have invested considerable time and money in IELTS preparation to earn bonus points. Statistics from the ministry and several universities show that these students are mainly from urban areas, particularly Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. In 2024, of 67,000 students submitting foreign-language certificates to be exempted from the English portion of the high school graduation exam, Hanoi and HCMC accounted for 21,500 and 13,100, respectively. Narrow the gap The ministry's proposal might upset students, but experts said the change would be nothing but positive in the long term. Pham Tan Ha, former vice president of the University of Social Sciences and Humanities, Vietnam National University, HCMC, said the change would help "narrow the inequality gap between students in urban areas and disadvantaged regions." Dinh Duc Hien, executive director of FPT Bac Giang Inter-level School in the northern Bac Ninh Province, pointed out that urban students have greater access to foreign-language learning environments and preparation centers and the resources to take tuitions and the exams multiple times. Hoang Phuong of the British University Vietnam said scrapping bonus points would end the anachronous situation of admission scores exceeding the maximum score, such as 31 out of 30 points. Foreign-language certificates would return to their intended function rather than being used as an additional tool for admission, he said. "It is a standardized measure of language or cognitive ability, rather than some kind of ‘soft power’ to bypass other core subjects." picked.t: 베트남-캐나다, ‘전략적 파트너십’으로 관계 격상...무역·AI·에너지 협력 확대
picked.body: 또 럼 베트남 공산당 중앙위원회 서기장 겸 국가주석(왼쪽)과 마크 카니 캐나다 총리가 24일(현지시간) 캐나다 오타와에서 정상회담을 하고 있다. 양국은 이날 관계를 전략적 파트너십으로 격상했다. /사진=베트남 연합뉴스통신 (호치민=베트남코리아타임즈) 응우옌 캉 (Nguyen Khang) 기자 = 베트남과 캐나다가 양국 관계를 기존 ‘포괄적 동반자 관계’에서 ‘전략적 파트너십’으로 격상하고 무역과 투자, 인공지능(AI), 첨단기술, 에너지, 공급망, 국방·안보 등으로 협력 범위를 확대하기로 했다. 베트남 공산당 중앙위원회 서기장이자 국가주석인 또 럼(To Lam)은 24일(현지시간) 캐나다 오타와에서 마크 카니 캐나다 총리와 회담하고 양국 관계를 전략적 파트너십으로 격상하는 공동성명을 발표했다. 이번 합의는 또 럼 서기장의 24~25일 캐나다 국빈 방문을 계기로 이뤄졌다. 베트남 최고지도자의 캐나다 방문은 1973년 양국 수교 이후 처음이다. 양국은 2017년 포괄적 동반자 관계를 수립한 이후 정치·외교, 무역·투자, 개발협력, 국방·안보, 교육·문화, 과학기술 등에서 협력을 확대해왔다. 이번 전략적 파트너십은 크게 8개 분야를 중심으로 추진된다. 양국은 △정치·지역·다자 협력 △무역·투자·금융·경제 △교통·공급망·인프라 △디지털 전환·AI·첨단기술·혁신 △에너지 안보·환경·지속가능한 성장 △식량안보·농식품 △국방·안보·해양·법 집행 △교육·문화·인적 교류 등에서 협력을 강화하기로 했다. 경제 분야에서는 베트남이 캐나다의 아세안 최대 교역국이라는 점이 중요한 배경으로 꼽힌다. 캐나다 정부에 따르면 2025년 양국 상품 교역 규모는 206억 캐나다달러를 기록했다. 베트남은 캐나다가 추진하는 인도·태평양 지역의 무역 다변화 전략에서도 중요한 경제 파트너로 평가되고 있다. 양국은 특히 포괄적·점진적 환태평양경제동반자협정(CPTPP)을 활용해 교역과 투자를 확대하고, 아세안-캐나다 자유무역협정(FTA)의 조속한 체결을 위해서도 협력하기로 했다. 양국 공동성명은 캐나다-베트남 공동경제위원회의 기능을 강화하고 양국 기업 및 지방정부 간 교류도 확대하기로 했다고 밝혔다. 첨단산업 분야에서도 협력이 확대될 전망이다. 양국 정상은 AI와 디지털 기술, 첨단기술 및 혁신 분야의 협력을 전략적 파트너십의 핵심 축으로 포함했다. 캐나다 측은 항공우주와 AI, 디지털 기술, 교통, 농식품 분야에서 양국 간 무역과 투자를 확대할 가능성을 강조했으며, 에너지 분야에서는 캐나다의 액화천연가스(LNG)를 포함한 협력 가능성도 논의했다. 공급망과 교통 인프라 협력도 강화된다. 양국은 해상·항공 운송망의 안정성과 공급망 회복력을 높이고 교역 확대에 따른 물류 수요에 대응하기로 했다. 특히 캐나다는 이번 정상회담을 계기로 베트남과의 항공협정을 확대했다. 이에 따라 양국 항공사는 국가별 최대 주 14회의 여객·화물 혼합편과 주 7회의 순수 화물편을 운항할 수 있게 됐으며, 처음으로 캐나다와 베트남 간 직항 운항이 가능해졌다. 캐나다 정부는 항공 연결성 확대가 기업 활동과 상품 이동, 관광 및 인적 교류를 촉진할 것으로 기대하고 있다. 국방·안보 분야에서도 협력이 강화된다. 양국은 국방정책대화와 국방협력 3개년 계획을 지속하고 인도적 지원 및 재난구호, 해양 법 집행, 비전통적 안보 문제 등에 대한 협력을 확대하기로 했다. 베트남은 캐나다에 상설 국방무관실을 설치하기로 했으며, 캐나다는 베트남 군 인력에 대한 교육 및 훈련 협력을 계속하기로 했다. 양국은 아세안과 인도·태평양 지역에서도 협력을 확대한다. 캐나다는 베트남이 2026년 CPTPP 위원회 의장국을 맡은 것을 환영했으며, 베트남의 2027년 APEC 개최와 2030년 아세안 의장국 수행 과정에서도 협력하겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. 양국은 유엔, 아세안 주도 협의체, APEC 등 다자무대에서도 공조를 강화하기로 했다. 이번 전략적 파트너십 격상은 베트남이 캐나다와 경제 관계를 확대하는 동시에 공급망과 첨단기술, 에너지, 안보 분야까지 협력의 범위를 넓히는 계기가 될 것으로 보인다. 특히 CPTPP를 기반으로 한 교역 확대와 직항 노선 개설이 함께 추진되면서 양국 기업과 인적 교류에도 새로운 변화가 예상된다.   <저작권자(c) 베트남코리아타임즈, 무단 전재-재배포 금지>

picked.t: Highlands Coffee founder repurchases controlling stake in deal valuing company at $800M
picked.body: The Philippine-owned Jollibee Foods Corporation said Wednesday that its subsidiary JSF Investments had signed an agreement to sell the stake in SF Vung Tau Jsc, the operator of the coffee chain in Vietnam, to Viet Thai International Jsc, a company controlled by Thai. Jollibee said the transaction forms part of its portfolio management strategy of building businesses, expanding their scale, and optimizing their ownership stakes once they are mature enough to attract outside capital. It expects to use the cash to reduce debt, reinvest in growth businesses, or return money to shareholders. After the transaction, Jollibee will retain a 49% stake in Highlands Coffee while Thai's company will increase its holding from 40% to 51% to become the controlling shareholder. The deal values Highlands Coffee at around $800 million, which Jollibee said is significantly higher than when it had bought the stake. It had paid $25 million in 2012 for 49% of the coffeehouse chain's Vietnam business. It also owns 60% of Highlands Coffee's Hong Kong operations. Thai told VnExpress in April 2025, however, that he remained responsible for operations and personnel management, and Jollibee was an investor and strategic adviser that did not participate in day-to-day business operations. With Jollibee's capital, Highlands Coffee expanded rapidly and became Vietnam's largest cafe chain. As of June, it had 1,062 outlets in Vietnam and overseas, both company-operated and franchised. Highlands Coffee posted second-quarter EBITDA of more than 1 billion pesos, up more than 70% from a year earlier and its highest ever. The brand has become increasingly important to Jollibee: its earnings rank second only to those of another chain, Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, and it contributes more than 8.6% of the group's profits. As it expands, Highlands Coffee is considering an initial public offering, expected in the first quarter of 2027.
